title: Don Lamond and Sid Catlett at the Howard Theatre
summary: Jones recalls Don Lamond and his girlfriend as the only white faces at the Howard Theatre, and how Sid Catlett brought him round.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Don? I knew Don as a kid. Don and his girl friend used to come to the Howard Theatre when it wasn't fashionable. They would be sitting there. I'd make sure with all my boys at Seventh and T, I said, "These two kids are going to come in." They would be the only two. They'd let them come through the block and they'd be sitting there, come back stage, go and get those hot dogs and we'd go to Chicken Charlie's and what have you - those two kids... the only two white people that sat in the Howard Theatre was Don Lamond and his girl friend that he later married. I didn't know that I was going to run into Don until years later, Sid Catlett - we were in California and Sid Catlett, and he didn't tell nobody but me, he had just had a heart attack and I was the one that was getting his medicine - and he'd come by a certain place where I lived. So Sid Catlett picked up Don Lamond when he was with Woody Herman's band. He said, "Come on, go with me," and when he walked in the room I was almost preparing to go to the tennis court. He walked in the room - and Don will tell you - he walked in the room and there was Sid Catlett and me. He didn't know what to do. We said, "Sit down." He said, "What am I supposed to do?
